Modern.tagline: A breathwork studio. Sit. Breathe. Leave.
Modern.brandNameRationale: The physiological sigh — a double inhale followed by a long exhale — is the single most evidence-backed breathing technique for down-regulating the nervous system (Huberman lab, Stanford 2021). Strongest of Agent A's evocative row: Holotropic Hour is Grof-specific and clinical-feeling, Prana Tide reads wellness-app. Long Exhale is two plain English words that name what every session ends with.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern breathwork in 2025+ sits between the Wim Hof imitators, the Holotropic facilitators, and the app tier (Othership, Open). The opening is a small in-person studio that runs short sessions without the trauma-release theatre or the ice plunge. Patrons are 28-45, app-tired, and want a room and a facilitator.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Othership (othership.us) sets the modern in-person template with sauna pairing. Open (open.com) holds the app tier. The Breath Center (thebreathcenter.com) competes on facilitator training. We sit smaller, quieter, and physiology-grounded.
Modern.positioningStatement: A small physiology-grounded breathwork studio. Sit. Breathe. Leave.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 45. Has tried the Wim Hof method on YouTube and lasted four days. Wants a room, a facilitator, and forty minutes after work. Skeptical of the trauma-release marketing.
behaviors: Books a single session, not a package
Walks from work; pays at the door
Sits twice a week and tells nobody

dos: Cite the physiology — vagal tone, CO2 tolerance
Publish the schedule and the facilitator
Keep the website to one page

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — LONG EXHALE set in a low-contrast grotesk, wide kerned. A single horizontal line beneath, suggesting the exhale, as the only mark. The line alone works as the favicon and the door plaque.

typography.primary: Söhne for the wordmark and schedule
typography.rationale: One family. The grotesk holds the studio register; the mono handles the printed schedule.

Luxury.tagline: A private breathwork hall in the Grof tradition.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Stanislav Grof (1931-2024) was born in Prague and developed Holotropic Breathwork in the 1970s — the foundational Western breathwork method. Strongest of Agent A's place row for luxury: Novosibirsk Method is geopolitically charged today, Rishikesh Pranayama reads tourist-yoga. Prague Breath is a quiet European address that the actual lineage runs through, and Grof died in 2024 making the heritage uncontested.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury breathwork is not the public-studio class — it is the private hall with a senior Grof-trained facilitator and a small membership. The opening is a discreet members' room positioned on lineage rather than amenities. Patrons are 40+, often have a therapist already, and want a serious holotropic-tradition facilitator in the city.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Grof Legacy Training (groflegacytraining.com) certifies the senior facilitators. Holotropic Breathwork International (holotropic.com) holds the institutional peer. Othership (othership.us) competes at the public-studio tier. We sit as the private members' hall.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A members' breathwork hall in the Grof tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 40 to 65. Often in therapy. Has done at least one Grof-tradition residential. Wants a facilitator in the city and a room that respects the depth of the work. Pays the annual fee without comment.
behaviors: Books a monthly session and a yearly residential
Holds the same mat in the cupboard

dos: Keep the door locked outside of sessions

Minimal.tagline: A breathwork studio. The schedule is the website.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: The bellows breath (bhastrika) is the foundational forced-breath pranayama — and 'bellows' is the English word for the leather organ that fills and empties. Strongest minimal mark out of Agent A's craft row: Bellows & Lung is fine but two-word, The Diaphragm Room is too clinical, Nostril & Cycle is too descriptive. Bellows alone — one word, one image, the entire practice in five letters.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal breathwork is a room, a facilitator, a mat, a clock. The opening is for a studio that publishes only the schedule and the facilitator. Patrons want what they paid for — a session — and nothing else.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Open (open.com) sets the minimal-app tier. Othership (othership.us) does in-person with theatre. Local independent facilitators compete on relationship. We publish less than any of them.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A breathwork studio. Schedule, facilitator, room. That's the website.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Practices already. Doesn't want a guided audio. Walks in, breathes, walks out. Pays the monthly fee and reads no marketing email.

dos: Show only schedule and facilitator on the homepage
Ring a bell at the start and end
Refund silently if the session cancels

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. BELLOWS in a single grotesk weight, all caps, wide kerned. No icon. The wordmark works on the door, the mat shelf, and the schedule card.

typography.rationale: One face. The door, the card, and the site all carry the same wordmark.

Corporate.tagline: Workplace breathing programs in the Buteyko tradition.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Konstantin Buteyko (1923-2003) developed the Buteyko Method in Soviet medicine — a clinically studied protocol for reducing chronic over-breathing, used for asthma and anxiety. Strongest of Agent A's heritage row for corporate: Grof Hall is more therapeutic than corporate, Orr & Leonard reads as a rebirthing studio. Buteyko is taught institutionally and lands as a serious B2B partnership; Agent A flagged the TM scope — used here as the method-tradition the group works in, not as the certifying body.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate breathing programs in 2025+ are emerging in the same window meditation occupied a decade ago. HR buyers want evidence-grounded, in-person sessions for stress, asthma, and respiratory health. The opening is a partnership group that places trained breathing-method facilitators inside large employers.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: The Buteyko Clinic International (buteykoclinic.com) holds the institutional method peer. Oxygen Advantage (oxygenadvantage.com) is the Patrick McKeown extension. Calm Business (business.calm.com) competes at the wellness-app tier. We sit clinician-led and method-grounded.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Workplace breathing programs in the Buteyko tradition, delivered in person.

targetAudience.primary: HR directors and benefit consultants at large employers, plus medical directors at integrated health systems. They sign annual contracts and care about evidence, attendance, and respiratory-claim reduction.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark — a single horizontal stroke with a subtle taper, suggesting an exhale — to the left. Reads cleanly on uniforms, signage, and procurement decks.

typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed quarterly letters
typography.rationale: Inter scales cleanly across procurement decks; the serif handles the printed letters.

Creative.tagline: A breathwork studio organised around the muscle that does the work.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The diaphragm is the primary muscle of respiration — the actual organ of breath — and it is the thing every breathwork practice trains. Strongest of Agent A's craft row for creative: Bellows & Lung is good but the minimal slot took bellows, Nostril & Cycle is too clinical. The Diaphragm Room reads as a designed studio that names the anatomy honestly, in the register of a good independent gym or a craft butcher.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative breathwork studios sit in the register of a designed gym or a craft anatomy lab. Patrons are design-literate, often work in adjacent creative fields, and want a studio that takes the body seriously. The opening is a brand with anatomical-illustration, slightly bookish identity that doesn't drift into wellness-clip-art.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Othership (othership.us) holds the design-led peer. The Class (theclass.com) is the adjacent body-practice template. Inscape (inscape.life) shaped the design template before closing. We sit warmer, more anatomical, more honest about the muscle.
Creative.positioningStatement: A breathwork studio organised around the diaphragm.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 42. Designers, editors, athletes. Reads anatomy books for fun. Will pay extra for a room that names the muscle honestly. Photographs the wall chart once and never again.
behaviors: Asks which protocol the studio teaches

dos: Commission a yearly illustrated anatomy chart
Print the schedule on heavy paper
Name each room after a respiratory structure
donts: Use stock photos of people screaming
